results.title: Derived data, figures and analysis code for calibrated Sentinel-1 detection limits before the 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, Nepal
results.author: Ajay Kumar Sah
results.text:
# Derived data, figures and analysis code for calibrated Sentinel-1 detection limits before the 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, Nepal

Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research). Published: 2026-09-09. Dataset. 0 citations.

## Abstract

Analysis code, derived figures and supporting data for a study of what routine Sentinel-1 products contained on the source face of the 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, at the last acquisition before failure. Three quantities are tested on a 500 m disc over the detachment — backscatter amplitude, interferometric coherence, and line-of-sight displacement from unwrapped phase — each against 120 control discs elsewhere in the same scene, matched on local incidence angle, aspect and slope, and against the source's own history over the preceding two months. The last usable descending acquisition precedes failure by 50.6 hours. This archive contains four Python scripts, three figures, one terrain geometry export and one seismic catalogue query. The scripts reproduce every reported value: coherence and single-pair displacement statistics against matched controls; the chained five-interval displacement test; track A amplitude under the incidence filter; and the coherence statistics computed at two candidate disc centres. All control-disc draws use a fixed seed and are deterministic. The Sentinel-1 products themselves are not included, being large and freely redistributable from their sources. The README gives the six HyP3 INSAR_GAMMA date pairs to order from the Alaska Satellite Facility, the area of interest bounds, the download settings, and both Copernicus Data Space evalscripts verbatim. Two inputs that cannot be regenerated identically are included: the terrain geometry export for frame 499, which was produced interactively from the Copernicus Data Space Browser, and the ANSS Comprehensive Catalog query result, since the catalogue is revised over time and one of its two entries was updated during the analysis. Expected output is stated in the README so that a reader can check their own run. On the source disc, 8,911 pixels at 10 m, with a median local incidence angle of 71.0 degrees and 24.6 per cent in radar shadow, restriction to incidence at or below 70 degrees and outside shadow leaves 3,945 usable pixels. The fraction of that disc below coherence 0.15 runs 4.1, 6.2, 1.1, 8.8 and 5.3 per cent across five quiet twelve-day intervals and reaches 18.0 per cent for the interval containing the failure, a departure of 4.57 standard deviations. Line-of-sight displacement across the 120 control discs scatters by 6.13 mm at one standard deviation and correlates with disc elevation at r = −0.72. The README records one defect found and corrected during the work. An earlier version of the coherence script gated the unwrapped phase on whichever coherence file appeared first on the command line rather than on the pair the phase belongs to, so its output depended on argument order. The version archived here matches the phase product to its own coherence file by the date-pair prefix of the HyP3 filename, and is invariant to argument order. Values of 6.17 mm and r = −0.75 in any earlier circulated version are superseded by 6.13 mm and r = −0.72. This archive supports the preprint Calibrated detection limits in routine Sentinel-1 products 50.6 hours before the Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, Nepal, EarthArXiv doi:10.31223/X5KZ3G. This is version 2.0.0. Version 1.0.0 of this record holds the derived data, figures and code for the companion amplitude study, Sah (2026), EarthArXiv doi:10.31223/X59N5N, and remains permanently accessible. The two versions contain different work rather than a correction of one by the other. Code is released under the MIT Licence and derived figures under CC BY 4.0. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2017–2026. Sentinel-1 products are available from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem and the Alaska Satellite Facility; seismic catalogue data from the USGS ANSS Comprehensive Catalog.

## Authors

- Ajay Kumar Sah (Purbanchal University): h-index 0; 0 citations; corresponding author

results.title: Sentinel-2 surface displacement and environmental predictor dataset for Langtang Lirung (2016–2026)
results.author: Pinglang Kou
results.text:
# Sentinel-2 surface displacement and environmental predictor dataset for Langtang Lirung (2016–2026)

Figshare. Published: 2026-10-16. Dataset. 0 citations.

## Abstract

This dataset contains Sentinel-2 imagery inputs, derived surface displacement products, analysis tables and environmental predictors used to investigate long-term glacier motion and pre-failure deformation at Langtang Lirung, Nepal.The dataset is organized into four archives:Sentinel-2 inputs for long-term pixel offset tracking (LONG), including near-infrared imagery stacks, Cloud Score+ layers, acquisition metadata and auxiliary data. The LONG series comprises 60 acquisition epochs from 7 February 2017 to 25 March 2026.Derived displacement, velocity and quality diagnostics, including cumulative horizontal displacement time series, eastward and northward components, along-flow displacement, full-period velocities, inversion residuals, formal uncertainty, matching quality, triplet closure and observational support.Analysis tables containing displacement and velocity statistics, spatial-block summaries, displacement distributions, change-point analyses, bootstrap results, stable-terrain diagnostics and image-pair network statistics.Multi-source environmental predictor data and associated tables covering 2016–2026, including ERA5-Land meteorological variables, daily aggregates of hourly fields, monthly climatology, Landsat observation records, MODIS-derived indicators and supporting metadata. Environmental records begin before the displacement series to support antecedent-window calculations.Together, these archives support examination of glacier kinematics, spatial and temporal displacement patterns, measurement quality and associations between deformation and environmental conditions. Displacement is expressed in metres and velocity in metres per year where indicated by the filenames.This release contains the LONG observation series and associated environmental data; the separate high-frequency (HF) series is not included. Quality diagnostics describe internal consistency and should not be interpreted as independent ground-based validation.

## Authors

- Pinglang Kou: h-index 15; 603 citations; corresponding author

## Topics

- Cryospheric studies and observations
- Landslides and related hazards
- Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Applications and Techniques

results.title: No detectable precursor in Sentinel-1 backscatter before the 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, Nepal
results.author: Ajay Kumar Sah
results.text:
No detectable precursor in Sentinel-1 backscatter before the 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, Nepal

# No detectable precursor in Sentinel-1 backscatter before the 26 August 2026 Langtang Lirung rock–ice avalanche, Nepal

 This is a Preprint and has not been peer reviewed. This is version 2 of this Preprint. 

There are no comments or no comments have been made public for this article.

## Supplementary Files

- Derived data, figures and analysis code (Zenodo dataset)

## Authors

 Ajay Kumar Sah 

## Abstract

On 26 August 2026 a rock–ice avalanche on the west flank of Langtang Lirung, Nepal, initiated a debris flow and flood that ran roughly 100 km down the Lhende Khola, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli. Several contemporaneous reports asserted that satellite radar had tracked a month of accelerating slope movement before failure. This note tests that claim in the amplitude record. Using Copernicus Sentinel-1 IW GRD amplitude on a single relative orbit, this note (i) locates the failure independently and (ii) tests directly for a precursory signal. Co- and cross-polarised change between 16 and 28 August is concentrated on the reported detachment coordinate: within 500 m, 30.0% of VV pixels and 25.4% of VH pixels changed by more than 6 dB, against 0.7% and 0.4% respectively across the remainder of a 308 km² scene. Across five pre-event passes from 29 June to 16 August, measured against 80 terrain-matched control patches, VV shows a nominally significant negative trend (−0.20 ± 0.03 dB cycle⁻¹ across independent control draws, p ≈ 0.02) that is produced entirely by the first scene of the series; excluding it, the remaining four dates are flat (+0.01 dB cycle⁻¹, p = 0.99). VH shows a monotonic rise (+0.62 ± 0.03 dB cycle⁻¹, p below 0.01, robust to exclusion of either endpoint) which is rejected by a same-orbit seasonal baseline: in 2025 the equivalent rise occurred earlier and had completed by late June, whereas in 2026 the face stood approximately 3 dB below the 2025 plateau at the same date and subsequently rose by about the same amount. The apparent precursor is the completion of a seasonal transition: a ten-year climatology on the same relative orbit places 2026 within 0.3 dB of the 2017–2025 median across the analysis window, and the July–August rise is what the median year does over that interval. No precursory signal is present in the freely available amplitude record at 12-day sampling; the detection limit is approximately 1 dB of progressive change over two months. Interferometric measurements reported subsequently indicate downslope motion of order 10 mm per month, an order of magnitude below what amplitude can resolve; the two results are complementary, and the amplitude limit quantified here is what separates them.
